purpose: Collect structured evidence from uncoached first-exposure adult learners without converting automated success into curriculum approval.
facilitator_rules: Do not define lesson vocabulary during the attempt.
Do not point to an answer or reinterpret a prompt.
Record every intervention, hesitation, requested clarification, and answer change.
Ask for reasoning after the learner commits to an answer.
Do not mark a cluster approved from this tool; route complete records to human curriculum review.

immediate: a safety, accessibility, or translation barrier blocks the attempt
the facilitator must teach or reinterpret content for the learner to continue
repeated: the same ambiguity appears in two independent sessions
the same visual cue misleads two independent learners
the same shortcut permits a correct answer without demonstrated understanding

clusters.title: Division, fraction meaning, and percent
required_prompts: Explain each idea in your own words without repeating the displayed memory hook.
Rebuild an example with different numbers.
Explain why one plausible wrong answer fails.
Name anything that felt undefined, abrupt, or dependent on prior schooling.
watch_for: hundred-grid legibility on a small phone
rate vocabulary adding load before meaning
confusion between the original whole and a changed amount
Spanish terminology that does not sound natural

clusters.title: Area and perimeter
required_prompts: Explain what each measure means without beginning with a formula.
Explain why area uses square units and perimeter uses linear units.
Rebuild a rectangle from rows, columns, and boundary segments.
Trace an irregular boundary without omitting or repeating a side.
Compare equal-area shapes with different perimeters.
watch_for: boundary segments omitted or counted twice
Spanish geometry terms that do not sound natural

clusters.title: Inclusive inequality language
required_prompts: Test the exact boundary and one value on each side.
Draw the allowed set before writing a symbol.
Contrast at least with no more than in a new context.
Explain what the closed point and arrow each communicate.
watch_for: symbol reversal after the visual is removed
the arrow interpreted as movement instead of allowed values
minimum or maximum used as an unexplained keyword rule
Spanish boundary phrases that do not sound natural
